knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Grit left on a wet floor is dragged across the surface by the mop and can scratch it, so dry soil is removed first.
Keeping the head on the floor stops dust being thrown into the air and onto areas already done.
A full or dirty head spreads soil instead of collecting it, so it must be rinsed or swapped before the next room.

practicalCriteria: Removes mats and loose items before dust mopping.
Keeps the head on the floor and makes overlapping passes without lifting or swinging.
Gathers the dust into a pile, collects it, and cleans the head before storage.
passRule: Knowledge checks: 80 per cent pass mark, so all three must be correct. The practical sign-off is separate, observed by an assessor, and is not shown by a quiz result.
evidenceRequired: Observed practical sign-off on assessor sheet
Job record or photo of the finished area
stopWorkCriteria: Dry soil lifted into the air near people
Dirty head used on the next room
Dust mop used with a damaged frame
